result:
**PR #1 review: the fix is complete and there are no merge blockers.** Codex confirmed seven findings, all in the tests and the documentation. Nothing was run; every conclusion comes from reading the code at base and head.

**Fix completeness: complete.** On base, `stream_close()` closes the stream connection's write buffer while `_error` is still false, so the compressor's unguarded `send_empty_frame` hook could still write into the closed `output_stream`. The new `_stream_closing` guard in `send()` and the wait for already-queued entries in `stream_close()` close that window. These paths were checked and are covered:
- client and server stream connections;
- the multi-algorithm compressor factory;
- the end-of-stream marker the sink sends on close;
- every close order, a peer closing during the drain, and the error path;
- sinks and sources used from another shard.

The parent (non-stream) client has no equivalent window. Commits 1–2 can be backported on their own.

**Confirmed findings** (Codex verdict `real`, all in scope)

| # | Location | Title | Severity | Why it is wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3 | `src/rpc/rpc.cc:562`, `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2010` | The new wait-for-queue step is never tested | medium | The sink's close awaits its end-of-stream `send()` before `close_sink()`, so the queue is already empty when `stream_close()` runs in the test. Removing or breaking lines 562–570 fails no test. |
| C1 | `doc/rpc-streaming.md:115`, `include/seastar/rpc/rpc_types.hh:340` | "Shut down only once both halves are closed" is false | low | The connection is also shut down by closing the parent client (`abort_all_streams`, rpc.cc:848), by the peer reaching EOF (rpc.cc:588) and by the loop-exit `stop_send_loop` (rpc.cc:1062). The same doc says so at line 49. |
| C2 | `doc/rpc-streaming.md:111`, `include/seastar/rpc/rpc_types.hh:387` | "Reading until it throws closes the source" is false for deserialization errors | low | When `unmarshall` throws inside `process_one_buffer` (rpc_impl.hh:941/951), `close_source()` is skipped, so `stream_close()` never runs. |
| C4 | `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2016` | Test never asserts that the hook fails with `closed_error` | low | The `try/catch` also accepts a successful return. Detection depends on the flush poller having run (10× `yield()` does not force a poll) or on a process abort at teardown. Use `BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW(..., rpc::closed_error)`. |
| C5 | `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2017` | Test can pass on base under one ordering | low | If the peer's FIN has already made the client loop set `_error`, the old `!_error` guard also refuses the frame. The test never checks that `error()` was still false when the hook fired. |
| C6 | `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2000`, `2017`, `2026` | An early test failure aborts the whole test binary | low | If a `REQUIRE` fails or an unexpected exception is thrown before `sink.close()`, the stack unwinds with the sink unclosed and `release_close` never set. The `SEASTAR_ASSERT` in `~sink_impl` (rpc_impl.hh:935) then aborts the binary instead of failing the test cleanly. |
| C9 | `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:1957` | `const_cast` on `this` in the const `negotiate()` | nit | The factory at :1801 in the same file keeps its mutable state behind a reference instead. The cast is undefined behaviour if the factory is ever declared const. |

**Unresolved:** C8. None of the three commits has a DCO `Signed-off-by`, which `doc/contributing.md:6-10` requires. Codex could not decide whether that rule applies to the GitHub PR route.

**Rejected:** C7. A comment at `src/rpc/rpc.cc:566` was claimed to misstate when `_outgoing_queue_ready` fails; Codex judged it a false positive.

- Coverage is complete: six review lanes, one gap review, and two coverage audits. The final audit found no gaps. This means the review protocol closed, not that the PR is bug-free.
- Missing sources: linked issues #3663 and #3653 were unavailable, and the Jira links were not fetched. The PR's own description was enough to establish what the fix must do.
